summary: Follow-up on the 2026-07-12 production incident where customer-facing requests experienced elevated tail latency and occasional request failures. Redwood and Polaris reviewed the root cause (KV cache growth and host CPU starvation during long-running prefix lookups), validated mitigations (runtime patch to bound memory/kv eviction, autoscaler threshold tweaks), and agreed on a staged rollout and verification plan. Action items and deadlines recorded.
topics: Root cause: unbounded KV cache growth causing CPU contention on inference hosts
Mitigation: runtime patch to limit cache growth and add eviction, autoscaler tuning, canary rollout
Reliability improvements: improved tracing, runbook updates, SLA/alerting changes
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-07-15
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Reyes (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Mason Lee (Redwood CSM), Aisha Khan (Polaris SRE), Diego Martinez (Polaris VP Eng), Lena Cho (Polaris Platform)

Summary (auto): Quick follow-up to confirm patch, testing plan and timeline after 2026-07-12 production incident.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Jordan: Alright, hey everyone, thanks for making time. we're gonna keep this pretty short, follow up from the postmortem we sent friday, just to confirm the patch plan and the canary schedule.
[00:00:12] Diego: Yep thanks Jordan, appreciate it. Quick note, we've got exec pain from a few customers so timeline is kinda important.
[00:00:20] Jordan: Understood. Priya, do you wanna run through the root cause recap and the patch we validated in staging?
[00:00:28] Priya: Sure. So root cause as we all saw is the kv cache growth — sometimes transcribed as "K V cash" in early notes — but basically for certain long-context flows, the runtime kept inserting large prefix entries into the KV cache and we didn't have a good eviction threshold. Over time that lead to CPU churn on the host because of large lookups and GC pressure.
[00:00:48] Aisha: i would add, in our env we saw spikes when a small percentage of requests had long prefixes and that pushed one pod to 100% CPU, other pods were fine, so it wasn't cluster-wide immediately.
[00:01:01] Priya: Right, and because the autoscaler was based on request count not cpu, the autoscaler didn't react fast enough. Also some of the kernel-level iowait increased because of large memory pages being touched during kv maintenance.
[00:01:16] Lena: There were some mis-attributed traces in the first pass, we thought it might be network, but grafana shows host cpu and the flamegraph points to the prefix lookup.
[00:01:27] Jordan: Good. So mitigation that Priya pushed, what changed?
[00:01:33] Priya: We implemented a hard cap on per-session KV entries, and an LRU eviction for the prefix keys. Also added an opt-in runtime flag to limit total memory used by the cache. In staging we saw the tail latency drop back to baseline under our synthetic long-prefix workload.
[00:01:50] Aisha: The staging test looked good, but we did see about a 2% increase in median latency for very large requests, which is expected because eviction adds overhead.
[00:02:02] Jordan: Can you remind everyone what build/tag that was?
[00:02:05] Priya: It's redwood/runtime:2026-07-14-kv-evict-rc1. We'll push a patched container image and detailed install steps.
[00:02:15] Mason: I'll put that in the slack thread and the postmortem doc after this call.
[00:02:19] [00:02:30] Diego: ok, so immediate ask from Polaris is: we need that patch, we need instructions, and we need a canary plan so we can sign off before rolling to prod.
[00:02:40] Jordan: Absolutely. Proposed plan: Redwood shares patched image and a helm/manifest snippet for canary. Polaris deploys to 10% of traffic in staging (or 1 pod in staging) and runs the load for 48 hours and monitors CPU and tail latency. If stable, then a 24–48 hour canary in prod at 5–10% depending on traffic.
[00:02:59] Aisha: That sounds reasonable. One thing — can we also get more detailed traces? The previous incident lacked per-request kv metrics.
[00:03:08] Priya: Yes, we added extra tracers to emit KV hit/miss and per-request prefix size. Those will go to the same trace endpoint; i'll share the dashboard link.
[00:03:17] Lena: Also can we get a dump on pod failure? last time we couldn't reproduce because the pod got evicted quickly.
[00:03:24] Priya: We'll include a transient heap/kv snapshot dump and instructions to capture it when a process crosses a threshold. There's a small perf overhead for the dumps but it's opt-in.
[00:03:33] [00:03:45] Diego: On the infra side we also want the autoscaler to use cpu-based scaling for the model pods instead of just request count. That should help faster reaction.
[00:03:54] Jordan: Sounds good, we can recommend a cpu target and add a short-runbook entry.
[00:03:59] Mason: quick note— we should also discuss SLA implications, because you mentioned exec — any customers impacted?
[00:04:07] Diego: yes, 3 customers had elevated error rates for about 40 minutes during the window, customer support handled outreach but exec is asking for mitigation and compensation options.
[00:04:17] Jordan: We'll put together an SLA impact note and suggested credits; Mason will own drafting that.
[00:04:22] Mason: Yep, I'll draft and share by monday.
[00:04:27] [00:04:40] Aisha: Back to the patch: one question — is the eviction LRU deterministic across nodes? we had mem pressure where different pods behaved differently.
[00:04:49] Priya: eviction policy is LRU with a nil tiebreaker; we also added a per-node seed so behavior should be consistent per deployment. but we can make it configurable if you want strict determinism.
[00:04:59] Lena: We'd prefer deterministic so we can reproduce locally.
[00:05:02] Priya: okay we'll expose a flag to set deterministic_eviction=true.
[00:05:06] [00:05:20] Diego: timeline questions — how fast can you get the container?
[00:05:24] Priya: We can cut rc1 today and a GA build after your canary passes; so earliest rc1 is 2026-07-17 by EOD.
[00:05:31] Jordan: And patch notes and helm snippet will be included.
[00:05:34] Aisha: For the canary duration — we want to run a sustained long-prefix workload similar to what tripped it originally, not just short bursts. so 48 hours is minimal.
[00:05:44] Priya: understood. We'll also share the synthetic workload harness we used, so you can replicate locally.
[00:05:50] [00:06:00] Jordan: Good. Anything else on mitigations?
[00:06:04] Lena: On alerts — the previous incident didn't trigger until cpu was already high. Can we add an alert on sustained kv entries per host above threshold?
[00:06:13] Priya: yes, we've added an alert rule: kv_entries_per_node > 10k for 5m triggers a P2. We'll share thresholds, tweakable.
[00:06:22] Aisha: Please make sure thresholds are visible in grafana so our oncall can see trending before it hits P2.
[00:06:29] Priya: will do.
[00:06:33] [00:06:50] Diego: Now, longer-term reliability improvements — any changes to recommended deployment for Polaris? dedicated pools vs shared?
[00:06:58] Jordan: Given sensitivity of tail latency to noisy neighbors and the fact you run high long-context workloads, we recommended a dedicated pool for high-traffic models. That reduces noisy neighbor risk and gives stronger latency SLOs.
[00:07:10] Diego: cost is a concern. what is the delta?
[00:07:13] Jordan: We'll send a cost delta with the suggested dedicated pool config. It depends on your concurrency needs; Mason will include an estimated monthly delta in the SLA note.
[00:07:21] Mason: noted.
[00:07:24] [00:07:40] Aisha: Another ask: can Redwood provide a script to scrub old KV entries from our existing cluster? we might want to perform a clean up before switching flags.
[00:07:48] Priya: yes we have a cleanup utility that can run as a one-off job. we'll provide instructions and a safety-check option.
[00:07:55] Jordan: Great. Let's recap owners quickly.
[00:08:00] Mason: I'll list them in slack after this call. quick recap: Priya build+image; Aisha run canary; Mason SLA draft; Diego confirm impacted customers; Jordan coordinate rollout and pricing.
[00:08:12] Diego: That works.
[00:08:15] [00:08:30] Aisha: One more technical nit — the prefix detection logic that marks a request as long currently counts tokens after tokenization. some customers use multibyte tokens and that skews counts. Could we add a byte-length heuristic?
[00:08:45] Priya: we can add a byte-based threshold as a secondary check, yes. we'll include that in rc1 as an opt-in flag.
[00:08:53] Lena: Nice.
[00:09:00] [00:09:30] Jordan: Okay let's move to timelines again and then wrap. Priya, you said rc1 by 2026-07-17 EOD. Is that still realistic?
[00:09:40] Priya: yes, barring any CI hiccups. If anything slips we'll notify immediately.
[00:09:45] Mason: And Mason will share the postmortem doc and open tickets by tomorrow 2026-07-16.
[00:09:53] Jordan: Perfect. Anything else from Polaris?
[00:09:58] Diego: not from me. Thanks for the quick response.
[00:10:01] Aisha: i'll follow up with details on the canary harness and the exact payloads we used when it tripped.
[00:10:08] Jordan: Great, we'll be on standby.
[00:10:12] [00:10:30] --- (fast-forwarding through 30 minutes of detailed discussion: config lines, helm snippet reviews, specific grafana panels) ---
[00:40:50] Priya: (reading) helm values snippet: replicaCount: 2, resources: cpu requests 800m, limits 2, KV_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES: 10000, KV_EVICTION_POLICY: "lru", DET_DETERMINISTIC_EVICTION: false by default.
[00:41:05] Lena: we want deterministic true in staging.
[00:41:09] Priya: will set.
[00:41:15] Aisha: on tracing endpoints — can you add a span annotation when eviction happens? that'll make it easier to search in jaeger.
[00:41:24] Priya: yes adding a span "kv_eviction" with metadata about size and triggered_by should be doable.
[00:41:32] Diego: and please make sure the dumps are redacted or run in a secure bucket; we can't leak PII.
[00:41:39] Priya: dumps will be to your configured S3 with KMS encryption, instructions include redaction notes.
[00:41:45] [00:41:55] Jordan: Alright, final recap of action items — we'll paste these into the postmortem doc and Slack.
[00:42:03] Jordan: Priya: publish rc1 image + helm snippet (Due 2026-07-17).
[00:42:10] Jordan: Mason: postmortem doc + SLA impact note (Due 2026-07-16 and 2026-07-19 respectively).
[00:42:17] Jordan: Aisha: run the 48h canary and post results (Due 2026-07-22).
[00:42:24] Jordan: Diego: confirm affected customers list (Due 2026-07-18).
[00:42:30] Jordan: And sync weekly for 3 weeks starting 2026-07-20.
[00:42:36] Diego: sounds good.
[00:42:39] Mason: i'll own the SLA draft and share with Diego for sign off.
[00:42:44] [00:42:55] Aisha: one last thing — could Redwood run a small benchmark against the patched runtime with the same workload and share the raw numbers? we want to be able to compare.
[00:43:04] Priya: yes we'll attach benchmark output with raw logs and the harness.
[00:43:09] Lena: Thanks.
[00:43:13] Jordan: ok great. thanks everyone for the quick turnaround. we'll follow up in slack with links and the rc1 build.
[00:43:22] Diego: thanks all.
[00:43:25] [00:48:00] Meeting ended.
